AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#674 @ 9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

A/B/C = 0/4/0

## Scope, independence and prior findings

Full-depth T4 review of the complete 2,128-line M1 diff, migration/down/backfill, scheduler wiring, owner controller, Stripe receipt listing, refund entry points, local ledger/transfer arithmetic, test harness and all changed specs; no candidate-source edits and no other PR audited. [Exact M1 candidate and size assessment](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5975772953)

No prior Sol APPROVE on original #641 exists to inherit; the refund/ledger code and relevant candidate specs are byte-identical to FIX ROUND 5 where checked, and this verdict rests on a fresh full-piece review and independent probes, not the other lens's approval. [Original Sol verdict](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/641#issuecomment-5972111823) [Original FIX ROUND 5](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/641#issuecomment-5972277703)

- Original **B-641-7 and B-641-8 narrowed close on their stated once-per-refund, 23-hour and cross-run fairness boundaries**: first-attempt admission is shared, expired work moves to review, and last-attempt ordering reaches waiting rows over bounded runs; this does not close the distinct-refund or webhook-mirror races below. [Current independent run and 35 passing candidate controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)
- Original **B-641-9 and B-641-10 close on the reported duplicate receipt and undersized receipt boundaries**: unique canonical receipt binding shares the refund claim transaction, duplicate assignments are refused, and an undersized receipt stays in review without recording. [Current controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)
- Original **B-641-11 closes at the specific reversal-attempt classifier**: Error.name, unknown provider code and invalid HTTP status are catalogued; the new scheduler is a separate unclosed text sink below. [Original nine failing-before assertions](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37144238446) [Current controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)
- Original B-641-5's package-create code is outside M1/M3 and is not certified by this job; C-641-2's release-composition condition belongs to the Money/API piece and remains carried there. [Original disposition and composition requirement](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/641#issuecomment-5972111823)

## B — must fix

### B-674-1 — distinct-refund transactions still lose one local reversal

**Piece alias of inherited B-641-12, independently confirmed, not a duplicate new issue.** `src/connect/fees/transfer-orchestrator.service.ts:224–228,253–277` re-reads without locking and writes the absolute `reversed_amount_cents`; `src/connect/fees/split-ledger.service.ts:134–147` does the same for `reversed_cents`, while the claim locks only each refund's own row. [Transfer implementation](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fconnect%2Ffees%2Ftransfer-orchestrator.service.ts) [Ledger implementation](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fconnect%2Ffees%2Fsplit-ledger.service.ts)

The independent actual-service overlap probe makes two provider requests for 100 and 50 cents under distinct refund keys, releases both local SELECT snapshots before the literal updates, and receives **transfer=50 / ledger=50 instead of 150/150**; this models the plain SELECT/literal UPDATE boundary rather than the globally serialized candidate double. [Executed counterexample](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)

**Minimal fix rule:** serialize the shared transfer and slice rows, in consistent lock order, or use database-atomic bounded increments with derived status/time; keep refund claiming and each local increment in the same transaction, and prove different-refund overlap with a real disposable Postgres concurrency test in an approved CI lane before closure. [Affected shared-row boundary](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fconnect%2Ffees%2Ftransfer-orchestrator.service.ts)

### B-674-2 — mandatory owner review/reconcile routes cannot be reached with an ordinary owner JWT

`src/checkout/payment-ops.controller.ts:110–113,582–624` mounts both new routes beneath `JwtAuthGuard`, `ServiceTokenGuard` and `RolesGuard`; the first two consume the same `Authorization: Bearer ...` value, respectively as a verified user JWT and the configured opaque admin service token. [New routes and inherited class guard chain](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fcheckout%2Fpayment-ops.controller.ts)

The native HTTP/Nest probe uses the real JWT/lifecycle guard with a synthetic verifier, the real service-token guard and the real role guard: the opaque service token is correctly 401 at JWT verification, but a verified owner JWT is also **401 instead of 200** at the service-token comparison; consequently the new 23-hour recovery queue has no normal owner-authenticated working path. [Executed HTTP counterexample](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)

**Minimal fix rule:** give these recovery routes one coherent authenticated owner path, for example a dedicated JWT-plus-owner controller, or independently authenticate a separate service credential without reusing the JWT header; never make the routes public or allow a service token alone to manufacture an owner role, and test owner success plus coach/student/anonymous/deleted-user denial through the actual HTTP guard chain. [Affected recovery endpoints](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fcheckout%2Fpayment-ops.controller.ts)

The class-level mismatch predates this diff, but it is a blocker here because the newly introduced mandatory financial recovery mechanism depends on those unreachable routes. [New review/reconcile contract](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/docs%2Frunbooks%2Frefund-transfer-reversal-review.md)

### B-674-3 — webhook-before-local-record makes the next refund settle for too little

`src/connect/fees/transfer-orchestrator.service.ts:216–228,258–265` adds the reversal after the provider returns, while `src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts:1432–1440` can already have installed Stripe's absolute `amount_reversed`; the newly used `owedHeadCoachReversal:622–635` then caps the next obligation using that double-counted mirror. [Transfer record](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fconnect%2Ffees%2Ftransfer-orchestrator.service.ts) [Mirror and new owed-share cap](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-dispute-handler.service.ts)

The actual-service probe seeds two legitimate 2,450-cent refunds on a 4,900-cent purchase with a 245-cent head-coach transfer and delivers each synthetic provider `transfer.reversed` webhook before its request returns: the first 122-cent reversal is mirrored then added again, the second request becomes **1 cent**, both refund obligations become terminal, and Stripe's total is **123 instead of 244 cents**. [Executed financial loss counterexample](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)

**Minimal fix rule:** distinguish canonical provider totals from per-receipt locally applied postings, bind receipt identity once, and make webhook/reconcile/request-record ordering converge without adding the same receipt to an already mirrored total; never terminalize a refund from an unverified/mirrored remaining balance, and cover webhook-before/after-record, lost local commit, full reversal and stale webhook order. [Affected admission and terminalization](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-dispute-handler.service.ts)

The old webhook writer is outside the own hunk, but its interaction with the new cap/terminalization is demonstrated unsafe for this piece, not a request to audit a neighbouring PR. [Current-source counterexample](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)

### B-674-4 — new retry scheduler logs arbitrary failure text

`src/checkout/refund-transfer-reversal.scheduler.ts:27–29` logs `Error.message` or `String(err)` verbatim; the independent failed-sweep canary reaches the actual Logger.error sink. [Scheduler source](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-transfer-reversal.scheduler.ts) [Executed canary](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)

**Minimal fix rule:** emit a closed failure catalog and safe correlation identifiers only, including a closed unknown fallback; retain actionable operator alerting without attaching the exception object, provider response, arbitrary names/messages or database request text, and retain the logger canary regression. [Affected text sink](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-transfer-reversal.scheduler.ts)

## Evidence, piece safety and limits

Final independent probe lane: **4 failed acceptance assertions / 35 passing candidate controls**, with only audit specs and the one-job lane wrapper added to exact candidate source; CI execution SHA is `0b135c0c2614ed66a0d91ecc8698f27562f5173b`, not a candidate approval SHA. [Final probe run](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171509961)

The first probe attempt had a missing optional test-library import and did not execute the new probes; it is not claimed as defect proof, and the replacement used native HTTP without any dependency/lockfile changes. [Initial attempt and passing controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37171379739)

The nullable migration/backfill/indexes are additive, include down.sql and contain no new user-id field; current M1 required checks, forward migration and schema parity are green, but these checks do not close the four demonstrated boundaries. [Migration](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/9a512028f49682073227c04ef1268c81102716fd/prisma%2Fmigrations%2F20270314000000_charge_refund_transfer_reversal_review%2Fmigration.sql) [Exact-head checks](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674/checks)

M1 has no import of a later piece and carries its own reversal tests; the operator's M1→M3→M4 land-as-one instruction and final green combined main checks still apply after fixes, and this audit is not live-provider, live-database or release acceptance. [Landing instruction](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5975772953)

AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#674 @ d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

A/B/C = 0/1/2

Lens AUD-SOL-CM1-117, agent 117. Independent full-depth T4 audit of the complete 2,983-line M1 piece, every fix-round source/test/migration/CI/runbook hunk, all reversal callers, owner HTTP guard chain, shared-row concurrency and recovery; no candidate-source edits. [Exact candidate/FIX ROUND 1](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5976568620)

## Prior findings and evidence applicability

No original Sol APPROVE is reused wholesale; prior closure evidence is used only after current implementation and relevant inputs were checked, with independent boundary probing of the new source-aware dispute path. [Previous Sol verdict](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5975860417) [Current independent lane](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)

- **B-674-1 (= B-641-12) closes:** transfer and slice compare-and-set updates retry a lost race without overwriting another refund; the disposable Postgres test forces two writers behind held row locks and passes 2/2 at this exact head. [Current live execution](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37175235299/job/111356379939) The same live acceptance assertions fail on the prior candidate. [Failing-before live proof](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37174064327)
- **B-674-2 closes:** the dedicated controller accepts verified owner JWTs, denies coach/student/deleted-owner/service-token/anonymous callers, and no longer requires two incompatible Bearer values. [Owner controller](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-reversal-admin.controller.ts) [Passing native HTTP controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)
- **B-674-3 closes on its reported refund/webhook boundary:** the webhook observes rather than increments recorded totals; refund claims bind receipt identity, retries persist the first amount, and webhook-first/full-reversal/reconcile/rollback controls pass. [Current handler](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-dispute-handler.service.ts) [Passing controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)
- **B-674-4 closes:** scheduler logs/Sentry use closed classes and codes, with Error/Stripe/thrown-string canary controls passing. [Current targeted execution](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)
- Earlier **B-641-7/8/9/10/11** remain closed on refund admission, paging fairness, unique receipt binding, undersized-receipt refusal and closed failure logging; **C-674-5** closes with `request_timeout` explicitly catalogued. [Current review/reconcile/once controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)

## B — must fix

### B-674-10 — the new source-aware lost-dispute path reverses the transfer twice but posts the head-coach slice only once

**Where:** `src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts:1124–1128,1188–1209` now passes a dispute source to the immutable posting writer, but leaves the final `ledger_reversed` flag in a later transaction; `src/connect/fees/transfer-orchestrator.service.ts:221–222,237–240,280–300` still sends an amount/cumulative-state key and unconditionally increases the transfer for an unclaimed source, while `src/connect/fees/split-ledger.service.ts:162–166` skips the already-posted source. [Changed handler](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-dispute-handler.service.ts) [Transfer writer](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/src%2Fconnect%2Ffees%2Ftransfer-orchestrator.service.ts) [Posting writer](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/src%2Fconnect%2Ffees%2Fsplit-ledger.service.ts)

**Executed counterexample:** one 2,450-cent lost dispute against a 4,900-cent sale with a 245-cent head-coach transfer first reverses/posts 122 cents; the later entitlement transaction fails and rolls its flag back, then a normal redelivery sends a second key (`...-122`, then `...-244`) and finishes with **Stripe=244, transfer=244, head slice=122, immutable head postings=[122]**. [Independent actual-service recovery probe](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)

Thus the head coach's ledger/Money keeps 123 cents while Stripe leaves only one cent; this is a concrete unsafe interaction of the **new dispute-source interface and once-only posting behavior**, not a blocker imported from a different PR. [Recorded recovery counterexample](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)

**Minimal fix rule:** make the source/receipt exactly-once boundary cover Stripe admission, `ConnectTransfer` and its linked ledger posting together: a durable dispute-scoped request/amount with bounded provider-key retry/review, and one atomic local source/receipt claim for transfer plus slice; a completed source must not send or add again merely because the downstream entitlement flag rolled back. [Affected source-aware transfer boundary](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/src%2Fconnect%2Ffees%2Ftransfer-orchestrator.service.ts)

**Verify:** retain `test/audit-sol-cm1-117-dispute-posting.spec.ts` unchanged (all four money measures stay 122), add overlapping deliveries and Stripe-success/local-record-failure controls, and prove the existing refund once-only and real-Postgres concurrent-refund controls remain green. [Failing acceptance probe plus 52 passing refund controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)

## C — carried, optional

- **C-674-6:** `refund-dispute-handler.service.ts:851,971–978` still lets a Stripe listing/send outage escape the reconcile method without an operation-specific recovery response; carry the prior optional follow-up to map it to a closed actionable 502/503 code explaining that no local record was completed and reconciliation can be retried. [Current reconcile implementation](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-dispute-handler.service.ts) [Prior optional finding and deliberate deferral](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5976568620)
- **C-674-7:** `refund-reversal-admin.controller.ts:49–72` does not forward the authenticated owner's identity, so owner reconciliation can send/bind money without durable actor attribution; carry the prior optional follow-up to record owner id/time/outcome and ids only in the audit record. [Current route](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/src%2Fcheckout%2Frefund-reversal-admin.controller.ts) [Deliberate deferral](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5976568620)

## Piece safety, CI and limits

Both migrations are additive with down scripts; the new posting table has forced deny-all RLS, a unique per-slice/source constraint and parent-slice cascade, and no new direct user-id field; M1 imports no later piece and carries its own refund/recovery/concurrency tests. [New posting migration](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/d93275469b0979c23431c94837043d379a6e9fe5/prisma%2Fmigrations%2F20270317116000_split_ledger_reversal_posting%2Fmigration.sql) [Current round and tests](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5976568620)

The original review migration retains its operator-authorized `20270314000000` name; the new `20270317116000` posting migration sorts after it, and final train ordering remains an operator deployment check. [Migration/ordering inputs](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5976568620)

All eleven required checks are green at the candidate, but it is behind main and this is not merge authorization. [Exact-head checks](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674/checks)

The independent one-job lane has **one failed assertion / 52 passing controls**, execution SHA `148ff7468371d06b53ce17e3a8586e863ae8f25e`; its diff from the candidate contains only the audit spec and approved lane wrapper, not candidate implementation changes. [Independent probe lane](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37177598709)

The new failure is synthetic-provider/stateful-database recovery evidence, not live money movement; the separate already-passing concurrency proof uses disposable Postgres, and final #674→#676→#677 land-as-one plus exact fee/recurring/dunning composition remains required. [Live proof](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37175235299/job/111356379939) [Landing instruction](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5975772953)

AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#674 @ 5bbcc92a5c47417c81d2c660654a738937332fec — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

A/B/C = 0/2/2

Lens AUD-SOL-CM1R2-117, agent 117. Independent full-depth T4 review of the complete 2,933-line M1 diff, every refund/dispute/transfer caller and fix-round hunk, immutable postings, source claims, retry/sweep/reconcile semantics, owner guard chain, migration/down scripts, CI concurrency wiring, changed specs and runbook. [Exact candidate and FIX ROUND 2](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5976957873)

## Prior findings and evidence applicability

No original #641 Sol APPROVE is inherited wholesale; earlier evidence is reused only on its stated boundaries after checking current relevant inputs and executing fresh independent source/recovery/time probes. [Prior Sol disposition](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/674#issuecomment-5976672242)

- **B-674-10 closes on the reported lost-dispute double-reversal boundary:** durable dispute-scoped amount/key plus an atomic local dispute/receipt claim covers the transfer and linked posting, so the unchanged prior entitlement-rollback probe keeps Stripe/transfer/head slice/postings at 122 cents; Stripe-success/local-head-posting-failure, lost-answer, expired-key recovery and overlapping-delivery controls also pass. [Current independent execution](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37183275202) The round's failing-before run executes the original assertion and all nine new candidate assertions as actual failures. [Failing-before evidence](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37179564456)
- **B-674-1 (= B-641-12) remains closed:** current exact-head disposable Postgres execution runs both shared-slice/shared-transfer contention cases and passes 2/2; the fresh adapted prior CAS control and candidate controls preserve both writers' cents. [Current live contention job](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37179756740/job/111369749604) [Independent controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37183275202)
- **B-674-2/3/4 remain closed on their reported boundaries:** dedicated owner-JWT routes work over native HTTP and deny nonowner/deleted-owner/service-token/anonymous callers; webhook-before-record/once-only receipt/first-amount controls converge; scheduler/logger/Sentry canaries contain no exception text. [Current independent controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37183275202)
- Earlier **B-641-7/8/9/10/11** remain closed for refunds on admission/window, cross-run fairness, unique receipt binding, undersized-receipt refusal and closed failure logging; C-674-5 stays closed with `request_timeout` catalogued, but the newly added dispute queue has a distinct fairness regression below. [Current refund review/reconcile controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37183275202)
- The B-676-3 writer fix aligns ordinary inline timestamps and preserves sequential dispute redelivery time, but concurrent first-close authority is not closed by the stale-read fallback below. [Exact changed writer](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/5bbcc92a5c47417c81d2c660654a738937332fec/src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts)

## B — must fix

### B-674-11 — the new lost-dispute queue permanently starves later recoverable reversals

**Where:** `src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts:800–828`, especially resetting `after` each sweep and selecting the lowest ids with a fixed 20-page budget; persistent failed disputes stay eligible forever and have no durable last-attempt/cooldown/fair continuation. [Exact dispute sweep](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/5bbcc92a5c47417c81d2c660654a738937332fec/src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts)

**Executed counterexample:** with the permitted batch limit scaled to 1, twenty persistent failed disputes fill the page budget and a 21st is recoverable; two successive sweeps each retry exactly the same first twenty, while the last dispute remains **Stripe=0/local=0 instead of 122/122** and is never selected. [Independent assertion and selected ids](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37183275202)

At the default limit the equivalent is 1,000 persistent failed disputes ahead of later work; unlike expired refunds, these disputes never leave automatic retry, so a new financial recovery obligation can wait indefinitely and never even reach its stuck-alert branch. [Queue and alert placement](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/5bbcc92a5c47417c81d2c660654a738937332fec/src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts)

**Minimal fix rule:** retain bounded per-run work, but add durable fair continuation, least-recently-attempted scheduling or an equivalent cooldown/rotation invariant that reaches every eligible dispute across bounded runs and cannot lose fairness on process restart/multiple replicas; extend the existing refund fairness design rather than restarting the lowest-id dispute prefix forever. [Current refund and dispute scheduling](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/5bbcc92a5c47417c81d2c660654a738937332fec/src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts)

**Verify:** keep the new fairness assertion in `test/audit-sol-cm1r2-117-boundaries.spec.ts` unchanged, add more than two page budgets, mixed persistent failures/successes and concurrent/restarted sweeps, and retain all once-only amount/key/receipt and refund fairness controls. [Failing fairness probe and controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37183275202)

### B-674-12 — concurrent first-close deliveries overwrite the canonical chargeback occurrence time

**Where:** `src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts:1273–1285,1293–1308`: `existing.closed_at ?? new Date()` derives the absolute update from an unlocked pre-read, so another delivery can prepare a different first-close time before either writes and overwrite the already-posted event afterward. [Exact close/posting writer](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/5bbcc92a5c47417c81d2c660654a738937332fec/src/checkout/refund-dispute-handler.service.ts)
